terra.problem: Bildad being one of Job’s three friends and Job having lost so much are facts from outside this passage and need references.
Bildad calls Job’s words a blustering wind, but the passage does not say he thinks there is nothing behind them.
The explanation states as fact that Bildad thinks Job is all noise. The claim that burden talk is Job’s side of the story also needs support from outside this passage.
The claim that asking for wisdom is common in the Bible refers outside this passage without a reference.
The cookie flip does not connect clearly to beginnings and latter days, so the joke is hard to understand.
Saying the ‘we’ is Bildad and Job narrows the group more than the text does.
The passage says the shoots are uncut, not that the plants look healthy.
The claim that locusts appear elsewhere in the Bible needs a reference.
The claim that fear appears throughout the Bible refers outside this passage without a reference.
Bildad does not compare the thickness of a web with a cistern wall, so that comparison cannot be stated as his point.
Leaving cookies at the door does not connect clearly to the plant being disowned, so the joke is confusing.
Bildad says others will spring from the dust, but does not say they spring up in the plant’s place.
Bildad’s last words are about Job’s enemies and the tent of the wicked, not joy.
